Description: About Care Access Care Access is working to make the future of health better for all. With hundreds of research locations, mobile clinics, and clinicians across the globe, we bring world-class research and health services directly to communities that often face barriers to care. We are dedicated to ensuring that every person has the opportunity to understand their health, access the care they need, and contribute to the medical breakthroughs of tomorrow. With programs like Future of Medicine , which makes advanced health screenings and research opportunities accessible to communities worldwide, and Difference Makers , which supports local leaders to expand their community health and wellbeing efforts, we put people at the heart of medical progress. Through partnerships, technology, and perseverance, we are reimagining how clinical research and health services reach the world. Prototype in the browser so decisions get made against something working rather than a static mock. Sweat the interaction detail: states, transitions, loading and error behavior, and motion. Own the look and feel of our corporate and marketing websites Keep the experience coherent across many concurrent initiatives and brands. Build with SEO in mind — technical SEO, metadata, structured data, and site architecture. Collaborate across disciplines and communicate the work Partner with web designers, illustrators, marketing, product engineers, web engineers, and DevOps. About the Role: As a Staff Full Stack Engineer (Backend Focus), you will build and operate the backend of a Web Analytics and AI portal. That includes the APIs that serve the application, the read data layer over analytical data, authentication and authorization, and the integration points with the services the rest of the team builds. The portal gives commercial intelligence to the people who make business decisions, through daily briefings, customizable KPIs, analytical insights, geographic exploration, and conversational analytics. This is a Staff (L6), hands-on individual contributor role on a lean team where everyone is Staff: a Staff Architect, Staff AI Engineers, Staff Software Engineers, and Data Engineers. Architectural direction sits with the Staff Architect, and the AI Engineers own the agents. You are the builder: you take features from the design doc to production, end to end, and you make them fast, observable, and reliable. Most of your time goes to writing, reviewing, and operating code, including the user interface when the delivery calls for it. What you'll do: Build the backend and ship features end to end Design, implement, test, and operate backend services against explicit latency, availability, and cost targets. Implement typed, versioned API contracts and evolve them without breaking clients. Own authentication, authorization, and multi-tenant access control across the portal. Ship features end to end, from the API to the interface, when the delivery calls for it. Integrate the application with internal services, including the agent services built by the AI Engineers. This covers response streaming, timeouts, cancellation, and partial failures. Own the read path and performance Own the read path over analytical data: data modeling, query plans, pagination, batching, caching, and consistency trade-offs. Set and defend performance budgets. Profile services, reduce tail latency (p95, p99), and optimize cost per request. Run load and capacity tests before launches, and use the results to make design decisions. Make systems observable and reliable Instrument services with metrics, structured logs, and distributed tracing from day one. Define SLIs and SLOs, alerts, and dashboards for the components you own, and take part in on-call. Diagnose and fix reliability issues, and lead incident response and blameless postmortems. Establish safe rollout practices: feature flags, canary releases, and fast rollback. Design and raise the bar Write design docs for the components you deliver, compare alternatives with data and prototypes, and escalate risk to the Staff Architect. Raise the team's technical bar through code review, pairing, and standards for testing, observability, and safe rollout. Use coding agent harnesses such as Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex as part of your workflow, and review generated code against tests, types, and contracts. What you'll need: Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, mathematics, or another quantitative field. A master's degree or PhD is a plus. Relevant experience designing, building, and operating distributed backend services in production, across coding standards, code review, build, automated testing, deployment, and operations. A track record of building features end-to-end and owning them in production. Relevant experience in software design for reliability and scale, on both new and existing systems. Deep command of at least one high-performance language, such as Java/Kotlin, Go, Rust, C++, or C#, including its memory model, concurrency model, and runtime. Ability to work productively in Python, the language of the current services. Hands-on experience with observability in production: metrics, tracing, logging, SLOs, and tools such as OpenTelemetry, Datadog, Grafana, or Prometheus. Proven experience with performance work: profiling, query optimization, caching strategies, and load testing. Production depth in distributed systems: timeouts, retries, idempotency, partial failure, streaming (SSE, WebSockets), and decisions based on tail latency (p95, p99). Relevant experience delivering full stack to production with TypeScript and a modern web framework. Day-to-day fluency with coding agent harnesses such as Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex, including critical review of generated code. Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to discuss architecture and trade-offs in depth. Advanced communication in English; Spanish is a plus. Nice to have: Experience with serving layers for analytical data (OLAP, columnar stores, semantic layers) or with data platform integration. Experience integrating applications with LLM or agent services as a consumer. Experience with B2B, multi-country, or multi-tenant products. Experience with cloud (Azure, AWS, or GCP), containers, and Kubernetes. More about you: You are a builder: you like taking a feature from a blank page to production and owning it from then on. You spend most of your time writing, reviewing, and operating code. You treat observability and performance as part of the feature, not something added afterward. You influence architecture with evidence: measurements, prototypes, and explicit trade-offs. You go from the API to the interface when the feature needs it. You use tests, types, and contracts as the guardrails for your code and for generated code. You work well on a staff-level team where everyone operates what they ship. Description: About Kadince Kadince (pronounced cadence) is a fully remote (must live in the USA) software company founded in 2013. In a nutshell, we build tools to help compliance and marketing professionals at financial institutions do their jobs more efficiently. Kadince has been profitable for several years (we’re fans of making more than we spend). We’re bootstrapped, which means we don’t have investors. So our owners answer to no one. And they aren’t just giving us commands from their vacation homes waiting to cash their next check. They’re fellow team members and in the trenches with us. Why We’re Hiring After our team members, our customers are our most important focus. As our customer base grows, so does our team. We’re dedicated to giving each customer the best experience possible, which means having enough people to take care of all their needs. We’re growing quickly and so are the needs of our customers. That’s why we’re increasing the size of our development team. Who We Want to Hire To be a web developer at Kadince we prefer you have 5+ years of experience. This experience has given you an understanding of basic database driven web applications and a proficient knowledge of the MVC pattern. You understand that software development is all about the end-user (again, we really care about our customers). You have a desire to continually learn and improve your development skills. We love giving team members opportunities to improve their skills, whether through online courses, workshops, or learning from others. You’re able to adapt quickly to new environments, are organized and focused, can look beyond current constraints (you know, forest through the trees), and can provide solutions to complex problems. Simply put, we need a problem solver, not a taskmaster. Our vision, mission, and core values should resonate with you. That’ll be crucial to your success and happiness if you join the Kadince team. Let’s Geek Out If you’re geeky like our dev team (hopefully you are), you probably want to know more about our tech-stack. Outside of our dev team, we’re not really sure what most of this means, but we sure hope you do. Technologies/Frameworks Ruby on Rails GraphQL Postgres Redis ReactJS Minitest Cypress DevOps Kubernetes Helm Docker CircleCI Other Tools Jira Rubymine Sentry Logrocket Wooly Bugger Our Vision and Mission Our vision and mission aren’t something we hung on the office wall and forgot about. Seriously, we don’t have an office, let alone a wall to hang them on. But our vision, mission, and core values sit on the desks of each of our team members. And we discuss them regularly in our meetings. Your goals and Key Performance Indicator (KPI) will be developed to ensure you’re working to help us achieve our vision and mission. Our vision and mission are what get us up each morning. They, in addition to our core values, help us make decisions. Vision - Setting the standard for operating a great software company. We’re big fans of author Jim Collins and his best-selling book, Good to Great (bonus points if you’ve read it). While there are lots of good software companies out there, we want to be one of the great ones. The first word of our vision is also significant. To go “high school English class” on you, the present participle “setting” illustrates that we’re not looking to set the standard and then be done, but that the standard is always moving and we’re always chasing it. We continually stop to recognize the awesome things we’ve done and then look for ways to do them even better. Mission - Building the best software for compliance and marketing professionals at financial institutions. As Jim Collins taught in his Hedgehog Concept (told you we think he’s great—pun intended), great companies need to determine what they can be the best at in the world and focus on that. There are so many things we could solve as a software company, but we’ve found what we think we can be the best in the world at and we stick to it every day. Our Core Values Our core values remind us who we are. They also guide us in the decisions we make. They’re listed in order of importance. If we have a question when making a decision about people, for example, we look to the core value above it to make our decision. Integrity - We’re honest with ourselves and others. People - We understand that people are the foundation of Kadince and we act accordingly. Care - We love what we do and do it consistently and intentionally to the best of our abilities. Remarkability - We provide remarkable experiences to all who come into contact with Kadince . Growth - We accept yesterday and improve today. What a Day in the Life of a Web Developer Looks Like Your day starts with a development team meeting where you go through announcements, sync up projects, and discuss any potential issues. After the meeting, you put your head down and work on your assigned tickets in Jira. You spend the first part of the day reviewing your notes and prioritizing tasks for the junior developers. You make sure that you and the other developers are working on the most important tasks first, but you’re free to choose which ones you work on. For lunch, you meet a friend at the cafe near his work. You haven’t seen your friend for a few months, so you talk about life and your careers. You can’t help but feel very lucky for the freedom you have to take a long lunch break and meet your friend, as he has to hurry back to the office and get working right at the hour. Back at home, you continue working on tickets in Jira. At one point a junior web developer calls you on Slack and asks how to fix an issue. You expertly show him the process and he thanks you for being so helpful. You notice that another developer has been really on top of it today, so you mention them in the company Slack channel and thank them for being so awesome. Many of your team members respond to your shoutout with party emojis and hearts. In the afternoon your team has a standup meeting where you discuss what projects you’re all working on and whether there’s anything anyone can do to help. Your leader points out one of the awesome projects you’re working on and thanks you for being so attentive to the users’ needs. After the standup you do some QA and manually test a couple of the changes your team made today. You write automated tests to ensure the functionality that was just worked on. You find one little bug, which you log and then fix easily. You finish up your day by taking a look at tomorrow’s schedule and planning accordingly. When and Where You’d Work and What You’d Work On Kadince is a principle-based company, which means we focus on principles, not policies. You’ll work with your leader, Aaron Venezia, each week to review your goals/KPI and what you’ve been working on. You’ll meet regularly with the Development team to learn, keep projects on track, and ensure that goals/KPIs are being reached. While we aren’t super particular about when and where you work, you’ll need to work around the schedules of other team members to ensure that goals stay on track and nothing falls through the cracks. Overall, your schedule needs to help you achieve our vision and mission and demonstrate our core values. After all, this is a full-time job, and we treat it that way! At Kadince , work won’t tie you down to one location. You’ll be free to travel or relocate as you get the itch to try somewhere new. Want to spend a month abroad, working from a hotel and exploring the rest of the time? Go ahead. Just make sure you have a reliable high-speed internet connection (as if you would go anywhere without it anyway) and turn on the blurry filter during video calls so we don’t get jealous. We seriously get jealous. One of our teammates recently had zebras running around in the background of a video call during a team meeting. Come to find out he was working from the deck of his hotel at the Animal Kingdom in Disney World. Even though we were jealous, we thought it was pretty cool. Who You’d Be Working With We have over 50 team members (which makes us really happy since Kadince was started by two people in their basements). If hired, you’ll probably work with each team member in one way or another. Some of the people you’ll work with most frequently are: Aaron makes sure that Kadince software runs smoothly and that any problems are addressed quickly and efficiently. When it comes to software wizards, he’s the Dumbledore of web developers (but really, he wishes he was Voldemort). He’s been here since nearly the beginning of Kadince , so he’s seen it all. Aaron loves to go skiing and mountain biking, as well as play video games and pinball (can you beat him?). He’s very proud of the fact that he’s his tiny dog’s favorite person, and he has a strange passion for curly fries. Bernardo (better known around here as Beans) has been a web developer at Kadince since 2014. He’s originally from Chile, but has lived in Utah since he was 12. He loves to code, play video games, spend time with his wife, kids, and dogs. He also loves to learn new things. If he could do anything in the world he would go to space (although technically that’s not in this world, now is it?). Luis is a senior web developer and has worked for Kadince since 2019. He likes to hike, run, and be outdoors. Luis is fun and gets along with everyone, so feel free to joke around and have a good time. Just don’t play Rocket League with him. He WILL beat you. Actually, do play, lots of the other developers do. And if you’re lucky, he might share his grandma’s tamales with you. Benefits Since we’re a remote company, we don’t offer office snacks and ping pong tables. But if you’re a fan of “core benefits” that bring great rewards and peace of mind, you’ll like what we have to offer. Competitive pay, 401(k) matching, generous paid leave, insurance (medical, dental, vision, life, short-term disability), and a flex spending account. Yeah, it’s pretty great... And we love to spoil our team. We celebrate big events with you, like birthdays and work anniversaries, so you can expect some pretty fun gifts. We once sent some high-quality lip balm to each team member so we could all play a prank on Scott, our Director of Product. We’re fun like that. And this year we’re giving every team member the last week of the year off (we like to spread holiday cheer). How to Apply Applicants who stand out are those who are interested in working for Kadince , not just applying for as many positions as possible or trying to keep unemployment benefits. We’ve seen it all. No kidding, we once had someone ask us in an interview what the name of our company is. Needless to say, we could tell that person wasn’t really passionate about joining our team. When applying to Kadince , please send us a PDF of your resume. The questions below are your opportunity to tell us why you would be a great fit for the position. Take advantage of this time. Seriously, sell yourself! Thank you for your interest in Kadince . We look forward to reviewing your application. This position is open to candidates living in AL, AK, AZ, AR, CT, DE, FL, GA, HI, IA, ID, IL, IN, KS, KY, LA, ME, MD, MA, MI, MN, MS, MO, NE, NV, NH, NM, NC, ND, OH, OK, PA, RI, SC, SD, TN, TX, UT, VT, VA, WV, WI, and WY. Kadince , Inc. is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. Salary: $70,000-$120,000 Originally posted on Himalayas

You will mentor engineers and provide constructive code reviews that improve both the software and the team’s capabilities. You will build and improve CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and deployment practices to make releases safer and more repeatable. You will partner with Marketing and other business teams to clarify requirements, evaluate trade-offs, and communicate technical concepts clearly. You will collaborate with engineers across North America and overseas teams, supporting effective delivery across time zones. You will work with platform vendors to resolve issues, improve service quality, and advocate for Dexcom ’s needs. You will contribute to planning and delivery, identify risks early, and follow through on production issues and preventive improvements. You will maintain clear technical documentation so teammates and new hires can understand, operate, and extend the systems we build. Description: About Kadince Kadince (pronounced cadence) is a fully remote American software company founded in 2013. In a nutshell, we build tools to help financial institutions track and manage the good they do in their communities. Why We’re Looking for Contractors As our customer base grows, so does our team. We’re dedicated to giving each customer the best experience possible, which means having enough people to take care of all their needs. We’re growing quickly and so are the needs of our customers. That’s why we’re looking for contractors in Brazil to help with our development needs, work on full-stack projects, and interact with our team in the US. Who We Want to Hire To be a web development contractor at Kadince you should have at least 1 year of work experience. This experience has given you an understanding of basic database-driven web applications and a proficient knowledge of the MVC pattern. You’re able to adapt quickly to new environments, are organized and focused, can look beyond current constraints, and can provide solutions to complex problems. Simply put, we need a problem solver, not just someone who completes as many tasks as possible. Even though you'll be working remotely from Brazil, you’ll be joining projects that may involve interactions with our US-based development team. So a strong level of English communication is important. This will make it possible to participate in occasional meetings to discuss project progress. Let’s Geek Out If you’re geeky like our dev team (hopefully you are), you probably want to know more about our tech stack. Outside of our dev team, we’re not really sure what most of this means, but we sure hope you do. Technologies/Frameworks Ruby on Rails GraphQL Postgres Redis ReactJS Minitest Cypress DevOps Kubernetes Helm Docker CircleCI Other Tools Jira Rubymine Sentry Logrocket Wooly Bugger Our Core Values Our core values remind us who we are. They also guide us in the decisions we make. They’re listed in order of importance. If we have a question when making a decision about people, for example, we look to the core value above it to make our decision. Integrity - We’re honest with ourselves and others. People - We understand that people are the foundation of Kadince and we act accordingly. Care - We love what we do and do it consistently and intentionally to the best of our abilities. Remarkability - We provide remarkable experiences to all who come into contact with Kadince . Growth - We accept yesterday and improve today. These core values should resonate with you. Even our contractors are expected to provide work that demonstrates these values. What You’d Work On As a contractor, you’ll work on various projects with the Kadince development team. Here are examples of projects you may find yourself working on: Software bugs Feature enhancements Feature creation You’ll work with your Kadince contact to get assignments, complete projects, and receive feedback. We’re always open to feedback and suggestions, so if you ever see areas of improvement or ways we might make your job easier, please let us know. Flexibility At Kadince , we understand that flexibility is crucial, especially for contractors. We offer the freedom to work remotely from anywhere, allowing you to set up a work environment that fits your personal and professional needs. Our team is distributed and accustomed to asynchronous communication, which means that even though you'll have to communicate with our US-based team, your schedule can remain flexible to accommodate your availability and your time zone. Compensation At Kadince , we offer compensation above typical rates in the Brazilian market, paid in USD—an exciting opportunity to work with a global team and gain valuable international experience. Here’s what you can expect based on your level of experience and expertise: Tier 1: Entry Level (1-2 years of experience): $5-$10/hour – A solid foundation to kickstart your career and make meaningful contributions. Tier 2: Mid Level (2-5 years of experience): $10-$15/hour – Recognizing your growing expertise and ability to deliver impactful solutions. Tier 3: Senior Level (5+ years of experience): $15-$20/hour – Rewarding your advanced skills, leadership, and significant contributions. * These ranges represent an initial offer based on your experience, technical skills, and English communication level. As you consistently deliver excellent work, there may be opportunities to align your compensation with your growing contribution to the projects. How to Apply Applicants who stand out are those who are interested in working with Kadince . We’ve seen it all. No kidding, we once had someone ask us in an interview what the name of our company is. Needless to say, we could tell that person wasn’t really passionate about joining our team. When applying to Kadince , please send us PDFs of your resume and cover letter. The cover letter is your opportunity to tell us why we should choose to work with you but should be no longer than 300 words. Take advantage of this time. Seriously, sell yourself! Thank you for your interest in Kadince . We look forward to reviewing your application. * This position is open to candidates living in Brazil. Description: About Us: YipitData is the leading market research and analytics firm for the disruptive economy and most recently raised $475M from The Carlyle Group at a valuation of over $1B. Every day, our proprietary technology analyzes billions of alternative data points to uncover actionable insights across sectors like software, AI, cloud, e-commerce, ridesharing, and payments. Our data and research teams transform raw data into strategic intelligence, delivering accurate, timely, and deeply contextualized analysis that our customers—ranging from the world’s top investment funds to Fortune 500 companies—depend on to drive high-stakes decisions. From sourcing and licensing novel datasets to rigorous analysis and expert narrative framing, our teams ensure clients get not just data, but clarity and confidence. We operate globally with offices in the US, APAC, and India. Our award-winning, people-centric culture—recognized by Inc. as a Best Workplace for three consecutive years—emphasizes transparency, ownership, and continuous mastery. From day one, you’ll take the lead on meaningful work, accelerate your growth, and gain exposure that shapes careers. Why Top Talent Chooses YipitData : Ownership That Matters : You’ll lead high-impact projects with real business outcomes Rapid Growth : We compress years of learning into months Merit Over Titles : Trust and responsibility are earned through execution, not tenure Velocity with Purpose: We move fast, support each other, and aim high—always with purpose and intention If your ambition is matched by your work ethic—and you're hungry for a place where growth, impact, and ownership are the norm— YipitData might be the opportunity you’ve been waiting for. About The Role: YipitData is looking for a Lead Web Designer & Developer to own the design and development of our public-facing websites. This is a hands-on role for someone who can move fluidly from user experience and visual design to responsive implementation in Webflow. You will establish the systems, templates, and technical foundations that allow our teams to publish high-quality content quickly and consistently—without relying on engineering for routine website work. You will help evolve our website into a scalable growth platform that supports YipitData ’s businesses, strengthens our brand, and creates clear, intuitive experiences for our audiences. As the company’s in-house website design and development expert, you will partner closely with Design, Brand and Communications, Demand Generation, Corporate and Investor Marketing, Product, and business stakeholders across YipitData . You will also help us build internal website expertise and reduce our long-term reliance on external agencies. Working hours: This is a fully remote role with a standard working schedule of approximately 9 am – 5 pm. Because you will collaborate with teams and stakeholders across both East and West Coast time zones, you will need the flexibility to occasionally accommodate meetings in a variety of time zones. This is a remote-friendly opportunity that can sit in NYC (where our headquarters is located), one of our office hubs, or anywhere else in the US. However, depending upon where the remote work is performed, income could be subject to New York State tax withholding. As Our Lead Web Designer & Developer You Will: Own the end-to-end design and development of YipitData ’s public-facing websites, from early concepts and user flows through launch and ongoing iteration. Translate business objectives, brand strategy, content requirements, and growth opportunities into clear information architecture and compelling web experiences. Design and build responsive, accessible, production-ready pages, templates, components, and interactions in Webflow. Create and maintain a scalable website design system that improves consistency, quality, and speed across YipitData ’s web properties. Serve as the technical owner of our Webflow environment, including CMS architecture, reusable components, custom code, integrations, permissions, documentation, and publishing workflows. Partner with Demand Generation and Marketing to support SEO and AEO, conversion optimization, experimentation, analytics, lead flows, and campaign launches. Collaborate with Brand and Communications to ensure that every website experience reflects YipitData ’s visual identity, narrative, voice, and editorial standards. Work with business and product teams to turn complex offerings—including data, research, and AI-powered products—into intuitive, credible, and engaging digital experiences. Establish website quality standards and conduct ongoing reviews for usability, accessibility, responsiveness, performance, and cross-browser compatibility. Manage website projects and priorities across multiple stakeholders, communicating tradeoffs and moving work forward in a fast-paced environment. Develop self-service templates, guidance, and governance that enable non-technical teams to publish and update content safely. Collaborate with external agencies and specialized partners when needed while steadily increasing YipitData ’s in-house capabilities. You Are Likely To Succeed If: You have 5+ years of professional experience designing and building high-quality marketing or corporate websites, with a portfolio demonstrating both strong UX/visual design and hands-on implementation. You are highly proficient in Webflow, including CMS architecture, reusable components, responsive layouts, interactions, and custom code when needed. You have strong front-end fundamentals, including HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and can independently troubleshoot technical and implementation issues. You have deep experience with responsive design, information architecture, design systems, accessibility standards, browser compatibility, and website performance. You are comfortable owning work from initial request through discovery, design, stakeholder alignment, development, QA, launch, and iteration. You combine a high visual bar with pragmatic execution—you know when to refine a solution and when to ship, learn, and improve. You are an effective cross-functional partner who can translate among design, marketing, technical, and business stakeholders. You use qualitative feedback and quantitative signals to improve user experience, content discoverability, conversion, and overall site performance. You communicate clearly, manage competing priorities thoughtfully, and take responsibility for outcomes rather than waiting for detailed direction. Nice-to-have experiences include: Designing websites for B2B technology, data, analytics, research, financial services, or other complex products. Technical SEO, AEO, structured data, content discoverability, or large-scale CMS publishing. Conversion-rate optimization, experimentation, analytics, and lead-generation workflows. Figma and component-based design systems. Connecting Webflow with analytics, marketing automation, CRM, forms, APIs, or other third-party platforms. Working with multiple brands, audiences, or business lines within one organization. Collaborating with (and eventually reducing reliance on) external design and development agencies. What We Offer: Our compensation package includes comprehensive benefits, perks, and a competitive salary: We care about your personal life, and we mean it. We offer flexible work hours, flexible vacation, a generous 401K match, parental leave, team events, wellness budget, learning reimbursement, and more! Your growth at YipitData is determined by the impact that you are making, not by tenure, unnecessary facetime, or office politics. Everyone at YipitData is empowered to learn, self-improve, and master their skills in an environment focused on ownership, respect, and trust. See more on our high-impact, high-opportunity work environment above! Base Salary + Performance-Based Bonus: The annual base salary range for this position is anticipated to be $150,000 with eligibility for an annual performance-based bonus of up to 10% . Final compensation may be determined by a number of factors, including, but not limited to, the applicant’s experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, and internal team benchmarks. This role may be performed fully remotely within the United States. Please note that our US headquarters are located in NYC. If the remote work is performed outside of these offices, income may be subject to New York State tax withholding. Description: Job title: Senior Full Stack Web/Mobile Application Engineer Department: Development The Role: As our agency grows, we are taking on more and more web and mobile application projects for our clients. Staying up-to-date on the latest development technologies and methodologies. Skills & Qualifications: You should have a minimum of 5 years of professional experience, preferably in a technical role and with agency experience. Full Stack experience with a variety of frontend and backend tools and technologies and their surrounding ecosystems is a requirement for this role. Comfort talking directly with clients about requirements, technical trade-offs, and project status. Description: Project Overview We are looking for an experienced developer to build a modern Showcase experience for the ResponsiveAds website. Description: Senior Full Stack PHP Developer — Product Catalogue & Quoting Company Mission At RestaurantSupply.com , our mission is to help customers save time and money when purchasing commercial kitchen equipment and supplies. We combine a customer-centric shopping experience with our industry buying power to make purchasing commercial kitchen equipment easier, more efficient, and more cost-effective. Role Overview We are looking for a Senior Full Stack PHP Developer to own the architecture and development of our product catalogue and quoting platform. This is an opportunity to build a new product from the ground up, establish its technical foundations, and shape how we manage and present complex product information at scale.The platform will power our product catalogue and quoting capabilities, bringing together product information from manufacturers and other sources into a structured, reliable, and scalable system. Your primary focus will be product information management (PIM), data modeling, large-scale data ingestion, and building a maintainable, monitorable, and scalable application. You'll design systems that can ingest, normalize, validate, and manage millions of product records while supporting accurate product information and flexible quoting functionality.You'll work primarily with PHP and Symfony on the backend, using caching, queues, and asynchronous processing to support reliable performance at scale. You'll also build web crawling and scraping capabilities, develop REST APIs, and contribute to a modern JavaScript frontend using React.This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll own both architecture and implementation, working alongside our existing developers and collaborating with colleagues responsible for reviewing product data. We're looking for someone who combines strong technical judgment with attention to detail, curiosity, and a sense of ownership. Responsibilities Architecture and Product Development Own the technical architecture of the product catalogue and quoting platform, designing for scalability, maintainability, reliability, and observability. Design robust data models for products, variants, specifications, pricing, configurable options, accessories, and discounts. Build and maintain the PHP/Symfony backend, including REST APIs and integrations. Establish development standards, automated testing practices, and architectural patterns that support long-term maintainability. Product Information Management and Data Ingestion Design and maintain data ingestion pipelines that collect and process large volumes of manufacturer product information. Build reliable web crawling and scraping systems to gather product specifications, descriptions, images, and other relevant data. Develop data normalization, validation, deduplication, and enrichment processes to create consistent, accurate product records from multiple sources. Design mechanisms to identify incomplete or inconsistent records, handle ingestion failures, and support efficient product data review and correction. Build scalable processes for initial imports, incremental updates, and ongoing product data maintenance. Backend Engineering and Reliability Implement asynchronous processing and background jobs using Symfony Messenger and message queues. Develop caching strategies using Redis or similar technologies while maintaining data consistency. Design robust failure handling, retries, and recovery processes for ingestion pipelines and background workers. Description: Satellite and drone imagery access is on the rise, and traditional image processing methods are struggling to keep up. We've never had more data, turning those pixels into trusted, measurable understanding still takes months of AI work. HUNTR™ reduces this to hours. We do not sell models. We provide the infrastructure that lets governments and enterprises build, validate, deploy and operate visual models they own. From pixel inputs to operational 2D and 3D outputs, under full sovereign control. Once deployed, every new sensor observation improves the customer's understanding of reality. Wherever the mission takes place, HUNTR™ runs there - from SaaS and private cloud to on-premise, classified networks and edge hardware in the field We kicked off in 2020 and have secured $35 million in Series A funding from a lineup of top US and European investors, among which Microsoft M12, Point72 Ventures, Maxar, In-Q-Tel, SAFRAN, and ISAI/Capgemini. The HUNTR™ workflow produces 3D outputs alongside 2D detections. Customers who need full simulation fidelity consume those through game engines. Design the interaction model for operational use: navigation, inspection, orientation between the 3D view and the underlying 2D data. Work with the teams producing the tilesets on what the pipeline emits, so the browser consumes it directly and rendering constraints are fixed upstream rather than patched in the client. Keep it performant on ordinary laptops. Tile size, texture compression, request patterns and load time are measured, not guessed. Ship one viewer across SaaS, single-tenant cloud, on-premise and edge deployments. Your Profile You have strong practical experience with Vue.js and building complex, stateful single-page applications. You have rendered 3D geospatial content in the browser with Cesium or an equivalent library, and you have worked with 3D Tiles or a comparable tiled 3D format You have solid software engineering fundamentals: HTML, CSS, TypeScript, component and integration testing, CI/CD, performance profiling. You are familiar with geospatial concepts: coordinate reference systems, raster vs. vector data, tiled data structures, GeoJSON. You consume REST APIs and manage asynchronous state against long-running backend jobs You have a strong sense for UX in technical products. You translate a complex workflow into a clear interface without stripping out its power. You are outcome-oriented and take pride in shipping interfaces that users want to work in. Tech Stack Node.js, Vue.js, TypeScript Cesium, 3D Tiles OpenLayers Cypress REST APIs Docker, Kubernetes Why join us Own the surface where 3D reaches the customer: every 3D result the pipeline produces ends in your viewer. Real constraints: analysts on ordinary hardware, on-premise and edge deployments, and a result that has to be usable the moment the job finishes. Diverse deployment challenges: ship a single application that runs in the cloud, on classified networks, or on a laptop in the field. Strong technical culture: work alongside 3D graphics engineers, ML engineers and GIS specialists solving novel problems. Description: Job Overview We’re looking for a Frontend Engineer to build resilient, responsive user interfaces and deliver high-performance web applications. The ideal candidate combines deep expertise in semantic HTML, CSS, TypeScript, and modern frontend frameworks (such as React, Vue, or Svelte) with strong capabilities in API integration, web performance optimization (Core Web Vitals), and web accessibility (WCAG). This role will collaborate closely with engineering leads and backend developers, establish reusable component libraries and architectural standards, and ensure seamless, high-quality user experiences across all devices and edge cases. Core Tasks 1. Interface implementation Build the screens and flows in scope from designs in Figma (or similar), matching them faithfully and raising the cases the designs do not cover. Write semantic HTML and maintainable CSS: responsive across target breakpoints / devices, correct across target browsers, and holding up as content changes. Handle the states that get skipped — loading, empty, error, partial data, long strings, slow networks — so the interface behaves when conditions are not ideal. Meet WCAG 2.1 AA / stated accessibility expectations: keyboard navigation, focus management, labeling, and contrast. 2. Component library and frontend architecture Build a reusable component library in framework, e.g., React, Vue, Svelte with TypeScript types, so the next developer is composing rather than rewriting. Establish and document the frontend conventions: file structure, state management approach, styling approach, naming, and testing strategy. Keep the component API small and predictable; document each component's props and intended use. 3. Exercising the API Integrate the frontend with the team’s API: authentication, data fetching, caching, optimistic updates, pagination, and error handling. Exercise endpoints against real responses during development — surface gaps, ambiguities, and awkward payload shapes to the backend team early, while they are still cheap to change. Type API responses end to end so contract changes fail at build time rather than in production. 4. Web optimization Establish performance baselines and hit agreed targets for Core Web Vitals: LCP, INP, CLS on target devices and connection profile. Reduce bundle size through code splitting, lazy loading, and dependency discipline; justify every heavy dependency added. Optimize asset delivery: image formats and sizing, font loading strategy, caching headers, critical CSS. Add performance measurement to CI or the deploy process so regressions are caught before release, not after. Deliverables Production-deployed frontend covering the agreed scope of screens and flows. Documented, typed component library with usage examples. Written frontend conventions: architecture, state management, styling, and testing approach. Automated tests running in CI. Accessibility audit results against WCAG 2.1 AA / stated with issues resolved or documented. Performance report showing baselines and final numbers against the agreed targets, plus the measurement setup that produced them. Cross-browser and responsive verification across target browsers and breakpoints. Handoff package: architecture notes, known limitations, and a walkthrough session with the team. Must Haves 3+ years of frontend engineering experience HTML and CSS — core, not assumed. You write semantic markup and CSS that stays maintainable past the first sprint, and you can build a responsive layout without reaching for a framework to do it for you. TypeScript and JavaScript — production experience with modern JavaScript and with TypeScript used to prevent real bugs, not to satisfy a linter. Exercising APIs — you are comfortable consuming REST or GraphQL APIs, handling their failure modes, and giving backend engineers useful feedback about what is hard to consume. Web optimization — you can profile a slow page, identify the actual cause, and fix it; you know what moves Core Web Vitals and what does not. At least one frontend framework — depth in React / Vue / Svelte / Angular or comparable. Which one matters less than knowing why it behaves the way it does. Nice to Haves Accessibility experience beyond automated checks — screen reader testing, focus management, ARIA used correctly and sparingly. Experience working directly from Figma (or similar) design files and collaborating with designers on the gaps. Familiarity with build tooling, e.g., Vite, Webpack and frontend testing tools such as Playwright, Testing Library. Prior contract work where you owned a frontend scope and delivered it independently. How we will work together You report to the Architect / Engineering Lead and coordinate directly with the backend engineer on API contracts. Written status update at the close of each week: what shipped, what is at risk, what you need. Code is reviewed by project lead before merge; you work in team’s repository and follow its conventions. Tooling: repo host, project tracker, chat, design files, staging environment access. Originally posted on Himalayas

Diagnose problems by reproducing them, tracing application behavior, and using logs and tests to understand what went wrong. Write and maintain automated tests, check user-facing behavior, and participate in code reviews with attention to accessibility, reliability, and protecting learner data. Help monitor and support our production systems, building toward taking part in incident response. Contribute to the tools and practices that make AI-assisted development effective at CDI, including project context, custom agents and skills, tool integrations, and agent-assisted code review. Document what you learn, communicate progress and blockers, and ask for help early when something is unclear. A working foundation in at least one programming language, and a project you can explain: how it works, the decisions you made, and how you investigated problems. Understanding of web application basics, including how a user interface communicates with an API and how an application stores and retrieves data. Ability to read and modify code, work through problems step by step, and test your changes to make sure they work as expected. Thoughtful use of AI development tools: willingness to learn how to direct them, critically evaluate their output, and ask questions when something is unclear. Clear communication and follow-through, including responding constructively to feedback, flagging when you're blocked, and knowing when to ask for help. Description: Description MEDvidi is an AI-powered mental healthcare platform setting a new standard for safe, effective, and scalable psychiatric care in the United States. We combine licensed providers with proprietary AI tools to deliver consistent, outcomes-driven treatment for conditions like ADHD, anxiety, depression, and more. MEDvidi 's technology automates charting, follow-ups, and treatment planning, freeing providers to focus on patient care while improving efficiency and clinical quality. As a Senior Frontend Developer on our AI track, you'll own frontend delivery end-to-end for products that directly affect how patients access mental health care and how our clinicians and staff work day-to-day. Your work sits at the intersection of a large, actively evolving Angular codebase and our AI-first product surface - patient-facing applications, internal tools for doctors and administrators, and the frontend for AI-powered features like our AI clinical assistant and AI receptionist. You'll work in a small cross-functional product team, taking features from requirement refinement through production release alongside product, design, backend, and QA. ﻿Why this role: Real product ownership in autonomous cross-functional team, you shape what gets built, not just how. Deep hands-on work on AI-powered clinical and administrative products, with AI-assisted development as a first-class part of the engineering culture (Claude Code, Cursor, and beyond). Modern Angular at scale: an actively evolving monorepo on the latest Angular versions, not a legacy graveyard. Responsibilities Design, develop, and maintain product features end-to-end within a cross-functional team, from requirement refinement to production release. Take ownership of existing Angular codebase areas after the departing engineer: understand, stabilize, and improve them without slowing down the roadmap. Write clean, maintainable, well-tested code: code reviews, unit tests (Vitest), and lightweight design documentation as part of the daily routine. Contribute to frontend architecture decisions and platform health: performance, framework upgrades, NX monorepo structure, CI/CD improvements. Drive AI adoption on both fronts: building frontend for AI-powered product features, and integrating AI tooling into the development workflow itself. Actively contribute to the continuous improvement of engineering processes and tooling across the community. ﻿This role is not for you if: You prefer strict role boundaries and don't want to occasionally cross into a SQL query, a backend endpoint, or the API layer to unblock yourself. You need a fully-specced ticket queue and a PM/BA translating everything for you You see AI coding agents as a novelty rather than a core part of how modern frontend work gets done. Requirements 3+ years of commercial experience with Angular(latest versions preferred). Fluency in modern Angular: standalone components, signals, current change detection and DI patterns, not experience from several years ago followed by a switch to another framework. Advanced RxJS and TypeScript in real production scenarios: confident design and debugging of complex reactive flows (stream composition, cancellation, race conditions, error handling) and fluency in a strictly typed codebase. Proven expertise in designing and implementing complex Angular application architectures at scale, module and component boundaries, decisions that hold up as the codebase grows. Hands-on experience with unit testing (Vitest preferred, Jest acceptable) as a regular part of the daily routine, not an afterthought. Hands-on experience with agentic AI development. For us this is a must, not a bonus: active daily use of coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, or similar), the ability to write effective skills, prompts, and instructions for them, understanding of the principles behind how agents operate (context, tools, feedback loops), and structuring code and documentation so agents can work with the codebase effectively. Comfort working across the backend boundary: writing or fixing a SQL query, adjusting endpoint validation, or tracing an issue through the API layer. You don't need to be a backend engineer, but stopping at the frontend border isn't an option. Intermediate English (B1+) and fluent Russian. Full overlap with CET working hours. Would be a plus: Experience building UI for AI/LLM-powered features. Deep understanding of responsive design, our patients access the platform primarily from mobile devices, and interfaces must be flawless across screen sizes. Proficiency in optimizing web application performance across different surfaces: patient-facing product and internal tools for doctors, managers, and admins (data-heavy interfaces, large tables and lists, real-time updates). What we offer High-impact environment: A chance to contribute to a product-driven company in the medical tech space. Growth & compensation: Clear growth opportunities and a competitive compensation package. Remote-first: Fully remote long-term collaboration under a B2B model. Health & wellness: Health insurance after the probation period, plus sports & wellness compensation. Career development: Clear growth opportunities, including personalized English lessons via Preply. Time off: 19 paid vacation days annually, 4 additional wellness days each year, and paid sick leave for the first 5 working days. Culture: Thoughtful gifts for key life events and offline corporate events. ﻿Ready to make an impact? Send us your profile, let's build something meaningful together. ﻿ MEDvidi is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and contractors. Description: Description MEDvidi is an AI-powered mental healthcare platform setting a new standard for safe, effective, and scalable psychiatric care in the United States. We combine licensed providers with proprietary AI tools to deliver consistent, outcomes-driven treatment for conditions like ADHD, anxiety, depression, and more. MEDvidi 's technology automates charting, follow-ups, and treatment planning, freeing providers to focus on patient care while improving efficiency and clinical quality. As a product-focused Senior Frontend Developer on our AI track, you'll own frontend delivery end-to-end for products that directly affect how patients access mental health care and how our clinicians and staff work day-to-day. Your work sits at the intersection of a large, actively evolving Angular codebase and our AI-first product surface - patient-facing applications, internal tools for doctors and administrators, and the frontend for AI-powered features like our AI clinical assistant and AI receptionist. You'll work in a small cross-functional product team, taking features from requirement refinement through production release. ﻿Why this role: Real product ownership in autonomous cross-functional team, you shape what gets built, not just how. Deep hands-on work on AI-powered clinical and administrative products, with AI-assisted development as a first-class part of the engineering culture (Claude Code, Cursor, and beyond). Modern Angular at scale: an actively evolving monorepo on the latest Angular versions, not a legacy graveyard. Responsibilities Design, develop, and maintain product features end-to-end within a cross-functional team, from requirement refinement to production release. Take ownership of existing Angular codebase areas after the departing engineer: understand, stabilize, and improve them without slowing down the roadmap. Write clean, maintainable, well-tested code: code reviews, unit tests (Vitest), and lightweight design documentation as part of the daily routine. Contribute to frontend architecture decisions and platform health: performance, framework upgrades, NX monorepo structure, CI/CD improvements. Drive AI adoption on both fronts: building frontend for AI-powered product features, and integrating AI tooling into the development workflow itself. Actively contribute to the continuous improvement of engineering processes and tooling across the community. ﻿This role is not for you if: You're waiting for someone else to define what to build,we expect you to come up with ideas, take them through discovery and development, ship them, and own the results after launch. You need a fully-specced ticket queue and a PM/BA translating everything for you You see AI coding agents as a novelty rather than a core part of how modern frontend work gets done. Requirements 3+ years of commercial experience with Angular(latest versions preferred). Experience owning a product end-to-end, including analysing the metrics that tell you whether it actually worked. Strong product and UX judgment, you can recognize when an interaction doesn't feel right and propose a better solution. Fluency in modern Angular: standalone components, signals, current change detection and DI patterns, not experience from several years ago followed by a switch to another framework. Advanced RxJS and TypeScript in real production scenarios: confident design and debugging of complex reactive flows (stream composition, cancellation, race conditions, error handling) and fluency in a strictly typed codebase. Proven expertise in designing and implementing complex Angular application architectures at scale, module and component boundaries, decisions that hold up as the codebase grows. Hands-on experience with unit testing (Vitest preferred, Jest acceptable) as a regular part of the daily routine, not an afterthought. Hands-on experience with agentic AI development. For us this is a must, not a bonus: active daily use of coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, or similar), the ability to write effective skills, prompts, and instructions for them, understanding of the principles behind how agents operate (context, tools, feedback loops), and structuring code and documentation so agents can work with the codebase effectively. Comfort working across the backend boundary: writing or fixing a SQL query, adjusting endpoint validation, or tracing an issue through the API layer. You don't need to be a backend engineer, but stopping at the frontend border isn't an option. Intermediate English (B1+) and fluent Russian. Full overlap with CET working hours. Would be a plus: Experience building UI for AI/LLM-powered features. Deep understanding of responsive design, our patients access the platform primarily from mobile devices, and interfaces must be flawless across screen sizes. Proficiency in optimizing web application performance across different surfaces: patient-facing product and internal tools for doctors, managers, and admins (data-heavy interfaces, large tables and lists, real-time updates). What we offer High-impact environment: A chance to contribute to a product-driven company in the medical tech space. Growth & compensation: Clear growth opportunities and a competitive compensation package. Remote-first: Fully remote long-term collaboration under a B2B model. Health & wellness: Health insurance after the probation period, plus sports & wellness compensation. Career development: Clear growth opportunities, including personalized English lessons via Preply. Time off: 19 paid vacation days annually, 4 additional wellness days each year, and paid sick leave for the first 5 working days. Culture: Thoughtful gifts for key life events and offline corporate events. ﻿Ready to make an impact? Send us your profile, let's build something meaningful together. ﻿ MEDvidi is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and contractors. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status. MEDvidi 's technology automates charting, follow-ups, and treatment planning, freeing providers to focus on patient care while improving efficiency and clinical quality. As a product-focused Senior Frontend Developer on our AI track, you'll own frontend delivery end-to-end for products that directly affect how patients access mental health care and how our clinicians and staff work day-to-day. Your work sits at the intersection of a large, actively evolving Angular codebase and our AI-first product surface - patient-facing applications, internal tools for doctors and administrators, and the frontend for AI-powered features like our AI clinical assistant and AI receptionist. You'll work in a small cross-functional product team, taking features from requirement refinement through production release. ﻿Why this role: Real product ownership in autonomous cross-functional team, you shape what gets built, not just how. Deep hands-on work on AI-powered clinical and administrative products, with AI-assisted development as a first-class part of the engineering culture (Claude Code, Cursor, and beyond). Modern Angular at scale: an actively evolving monorepo on the latest Angular versions, not a legacy graveyard. Responsibilities Design, develop, and maintain product features end-to-end within a cross-functional team, from requirement refinement to production release. Take ownership of existing Angular codebase areas after the departing engineer: understand, stabilize, and improve them without slowing down the roadmap. Write clean, maintainable, well-tested code: code reviews, unit tests (Vitest), and lightweight design documentation as part of the daily routine. Contribute to frontend architecture decisions and platform health: performance, framework upgrades, NX monorepo structure, CI/CD improvements. Drive AI adoption on both fronts: building frontend for AI-powered product features, and integrating AI tooling into the development workflow itself. Actively contribute to the continuous improvement of engineering processes and tooling across the community. ﻿This role is not for you if: You're waiting for someone else to define what to build,we expect you to come up with ideas, take them through discovery and development, ship them, and own the results after launch. You need a fully-specced ticket queue and a PM/BA translating everything for you You see AI coding agents as a novelty rather than a core part of how modern frontend work gets done. Requirements 3+ years of commercial experience with Angular(latest versions preferred). Experience owning a product end-to-end, including analysing the metrics that tell you whether it actually worked. Strong product and UX judgment, you can recognize when an interaction doesn't feel right and propose a better solution. Fluency in modern Angular: standalone components, signals, current change detection and DI patterns, not experience from several years ago followed by a switch to another framework. Advanced RxJS and TypeScript in real production scenarios: confident design and debugging of complex reactive flows (stream composition, cancellation, race conditions, error handling) and fluency in a strictly typed codebase. Proven expertise in designing and implementing complex Angular application architectures at scale, module and component boundaries, decisions that hold up as the codebase grows. Hands-on experience with unit testing (Vitest preferred, Jest acceptable) as a regular part of the daily routine, not an afterthought. Hands-on experience with agentic AI development. For us this is a must, not a bonus: active daily use of coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, or similar), the ability to write effective skills, prompts, and instructions for them, understanding of the principles behind how agents operate (context, tools, feedback loops), and structuring code and documentation so agents can work with the codebase effectively. Deep understanding of responsive design, our patients access the platform primarily from mobile devices, and interfaces must be flawless across screen sizes. Proficiency in optimizing web application performance across different surfaces: patient-facing product and internal tools for doctors, managers, and admins (data-heavy interfaces, large tables and lists, real-time updates). Description: Description Coralogix is a modern, full-stack observability platform transforming how businesses process and understand their data. Our unique architecture powers in-stream analytics without reliance on expensive indexing or hot storage. We specialize in comprehensive monitoring of logs, metrics, trace and security events with features such as APM, RUM, SIEM, Kubernetes monitoring and more, all enhancing operational efficiency and reducing observability spend by up to 70%. About Our Squad We're building some of the most important user experiences in Coralogix . Our team owns the frontend experience for products like Explore, APM, and RUM - interfaces engineers rely on every day to investigate, debug, and understand their systems. Although we're frontend-focused, we're a full-stack product team . We own features end-to-end, from product discussions and UX decisions to architecture, implementation, backend integrations, and production. Engineers on our team don't just implement designs - they help define the product, challenge assumptions, make technical decisions, and shape how users experience Coralogix . We're looking for a Senior Frontend Engineer who is a builder at heart: someone who can own complex problems, navigate ambiguity, make strong technical and product decisions, and raise the engineering bar around them. Work Location: 100% Remote. Candidates must be legally based in a European country. Responsibilities Own complex product features and technical initiatives from idea to production. Design and build intuitive, high-performance user experiences using Angular. Drive frontend architecture and technical decisions with scalability, maintainability, performance, and user experience in mind. Collaborate closely with Product, Design, Backend, and other engineers to shape solutions - not just implement requirements. Translate complex technical concepts and large amounts of data into simple, elegant user experiences. Proactively identify opportunities to improve the product, architecture, and engineering practices. Write clean, well-tested, production-ready code. Review code, mentor engineers, and help raise the technical level of the team. Use AI-assisted development effectively to accelerate delivery while maintaining high engineering standards. We're Looking For Someone Who Loves building products , not just writing code. Takes end-to-end ownership and drives complex work to completion. Has strong technical judgment and makes thoughtful architectural tradeoffs. Cares deeply about UI/UX, performance, and product quality. Is comfortable with ambiguity and challenges ideas constructively. Works effectively across Product, Design, Backend, and Engineering. Helps other engineers grow and continuously raises the bar around them. Requirements 7+ years of professional frontend development experience , including ownership of complex production applications. Strong experience with a major frontend framework ( Angular, React, or Vue ). Strong proficiency in TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML and CSS/SCSS. Experience designing scalable frontend architectures and building complex, data-intensive applications. Strong understanding of browser fundamentals, frontend performance, and modern web development practices. Strong understanding of UI/UX principles and attention to detail. Experience with APIs, state management, testing, and modern frontend development workflows. Strong problem-solving skills and ability to independently lead complex technical work. Strong communication skills and experience working in cross-functional teams. ﻿Nice to Have Experience with Angular and large-scale Angular applications. Experience with monorepos and tools such as Nx . Experience with observability platforms, developer tools, or large-scale SaaS products. Experience with frontend performance optimization and data-intensive UIs. Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS or GCP. Familiarity with backend technologies and distributed systems. Experience with AI-assisted development tools and workflows. Cultural Fit We’re seeking candidates who are hungry, humble, and smart. Coralogix fosters a culture of innovation and continuous learning, where team members are encouraged to challenge the status quo and contribute to our shared mission. If you thrive in dynamic environments and are eager to shape the future of observability solutions, we’d love to hear from you. Coralogix is an equal opportunity employer and encourages applicants from all backgrounds to apply. Originally posted on Himalayas

Description: UI/UX Frontend Developer DISHER is currently partnering with a global supply chain solutions organization on their UI/UX Frontend Developer opportunity. In this role, you will design and develop user-centered interfaces for the company and their internal applications. You will help translate complex service-supply-chain data and operational workflows into accessible, responsive and reliable digital experiences for internal and external users. You will own front-end implementation and user experience from workflow discovery and interaction design through production delivery, testing, performance and ongoing improvement. What it's like to work here: This organization empowers high-performance teams to solve complex global challenges through creativity, partnership, and technology. Employees enjoy a supportive, collaborative environment where initiative and growth are celebrated. What you will get to do: User Experience and Interaction Design Map user journeys and operational workflows and create wireframes, user flows, and interactive prototypes that make complex information easy to understand and act on. Gather input from internal and external users through interviews, usability testing, and feedback review and incorporate findings into product improvements. Explain and document UI/UX decisions for technical and non-technical stakeholders. Frontend Application Development Design, build, and maintain production user interfaces within the companies platform using Next.js App Router, React, and TypeScript, using React Server Components by default and client components when browser functionality requires them. Develop and maintain inventory and network views, on-time performance dashboards, filter toolbars, saved views, data tables, and analytical charts. Shape URL-driven filters, sorting, and pagination so saved links remain reliable and recoverable. Implement screens, forms, and data views across .NET and Next.js applications with consistent, accessible, and usable interaction patterns. Design System, Accessibility, Quality, and Performance Apply and extend the product design system, including Tailwind CSS, shared primitives, and design tokens, to maintain consistency across Navigator and related applications. Ensure responsive layouts, semantic markup, keyboard navigation, screen-reader compatibility, efficient rendering, and appropriately sized client bundles. Write and maintain component tests and browser end-to-end tests using Playwright or equivalent tools. Monitor and improve browser-level quality and performance for interactive, data-heavy pages. Collaboration and Technical Leadership Partner with Product, Design, Backend, and Data Engineering teams to translate operational requirements into clear and usable interfaces. Provide technical guidance and mentorship to frontend engineers through code reviews and knowledge-sharing sessions. Help define and enforce frontend standards, including component boundaries, TypeScript contracts, accessibility requirements, and review quality. Assist with scoping and estimating frontend work for sprint planning and product roadmaps. Stay current with React, Next.js, user-experience practices, and web-platform changes and recommend adoption when it improves the product. What will make you successful: 4-6 years of experience as a Frontend, UI/UX, or Full Stack Engineer with substantial ownership of production user interfaces. Strong hands-on experience with React and TypeScript in a modern framework; Next.js App Router is strongly preferred. Experience building complex tables, filters, dashboards, and charts rather than only marketing or form-centered pages. Practical experience with a utility-first CSS system such as Tailwind and working within an established design system. Solid understanding of server-side and client-side rendering, data fetching, rendering performance, and client-bundle optimization. Experience delivering semantic, keyboard-accessible, and screen-reader-friendly interfaces. Experience with Git, code review, CI practices, component testing with Vitest, Jest, or similar tools, and browser end-to-end testing with Playwright or equivalent tools. Experience mentoring engineers, leading small technical initiatives, or serving as a project point of contact; formal management experience is not required. Ability to explain UI/UX and interaction decisions to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Experience designing user-centered interfaces, creating wireframes, user flows, and interactive prototypes in Figma or a similar tool, and validating designs through user research or usability testing. Must have the current and continuing right to work in the United States of America without restrictions or expirations. Originally posted on Himalayas
